items.title: Live: Iran opens fire on ships travelling through Strait of Hormuz
items.description: The two Indian-flagged vessels reported being fired upon by gunboats from Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps, just a day after the strait was declared open by Iran's foreign minister. Follow live.

items.title: Donald Trump might have annoyed the only ally who can help clear sea mines
items.description: The prospect of mines in the Strait of Hormuz has highlighted a gap in US naval capabilities and reinforced its need for NATO help.

items.title: Iran's reclosure of the Strait of Hormuz 'disappointing', Marles says
items.description: The deputy prime minister says "every diplomatic angle" should be used to secure a permanent ceasefire in the Middle East.

items.title: Who's really behind 'Big Australia'? Taylor's high immigration stance raises eyebrows
items.description: Angus Taylor's criticism of high immigration puts a strange spotlight on his own party's policy legacy.

items.title: The quiet disappearance of Australia's rainfall observation network
items.description: For more than 60 years, Frank Pritchard has diligently checked the weather, adding to a record that stretches back more than a century. But he's part of a quietly shrinking network of observers around Australia. Without it, scientists say we risk missing out on important information that could help improve weather forecast models and climate projections.

items.title: The mystery of an outback 'catch and kill' squad during WWII has been solved
items.description: In the 1940s, a shadowy military unit was assembled to catch and kill Japanese soldiers on Australia's remote northern coast. The identity of the so-called Solomons Six was a mystery — until now.

items.title: How Trump turned on the first US-born Pope
items.description: US President Donald Trump described Pope Leo XIV's accession to the papacy as a meaningful moment for America. But now he has said the pontiff is hurting the Catholic Church, and is weak. Here's how their relationship has developed over the past year.

items.title: Andrew and Tristan Tate's renewed defamation claim names Australian YouTuber
items.description: An Adelaide YouTuber has been identified in a renewed defamation lawsuit self-described misogynist Andrew Tate and his brother Tristan have lodged with a US court against some of their online critics.

items.title: The myths of motherhood and the damage they do
items.description: I traced my family's maternal line from a home for abandoned children in Italy to my own wheelchair, confronting the myths we cling to about what makes a good mother — and the damage they do.

items.title: Crackdown on unregistered NDIS providers coming in bid to save $6b a year
items.description: NDIS Minister Mark Butler will announce reforms to the disability scheme on Wednesday that will aim to save more than $6 billion a year by 2035 — and the largely unregulated market of NDIS providers is at the top of his reform list.

items.title: Automation is growing in Australia's mining industry — but what are the costs?
items.description: At Australia's largest gold mine, drivers are more likely to be found in a control room than a cabin, but researchers and unions say jobs and safety remain significant concerns.

items.title: Valuables stolen from boots of shipped cars, victims say police won't investigate
items.description: Elihu and Amanda De Valle say thousands of dollars worth of their belongings were stolen from the boot of their car when it was shipped from Melbourne to Perth, but police aren't able to investigate.

items.title: Supernova Comic Con to open for second day after 'appalling' death of attendee
items.description: Organisers say a minute of silence will be held at midday for the family and friends of the victims before the event opens for another day.

items.title: Devils coach a psychic medium who leans into the 'witchy stuff'
items.description: Georgia Walker describes herself as a psychic medium, which she combines with her skills as a counsellor and teacher, as head coach of the Tasmania Devils' women's VFL team.

items.title: Remote communities appeal for place on government's fuel priority list
items.description: Remote communities are calling for assurance on fuel security in the face of potential shortages, along with financial assistance as already-high fuel and food prices continue to climb.

items.title: Hospital staff using ChatGPT to calculate medication doses, nurses claim
items.description: Whistleblowers say understaffing at the Northern Territory's busiest hospital is forcing nurses to take on unsafe patient loads, and some are teaching themselves medical procedures via YouTube.

items.title: Doing disco or school pick-up, Jessie Ware is having more fun than ever
items.description: Whether making opulent, grown-up disco-pop or doing school pick-up, the glam British artist is having more fun than ever.

items.title: Top national park in NSW revealed as state hits record number of visits
items.description: The latest NSW National Parks and Wildlife Service Park Visitation Survey shows there were 65.5 million visits to the state's parks over the 2024-25 financial year.

items.title: Out at sea, 400 million barrels of oil buffer Japan from the fuel crisis
items.description: Japan has oil stockpile sites littered around the country, and as the world faces a fuel crisis, neighbours in Asia have been turning to Tokyo for assistance.

items.title: The skis being made from three types of Australian-grown timber
items.description: A couple in the NSW Snowy Mountains makes skis entirely from Australian-grown timber, though manufacturing for the snow industry in a "summer country" comes with its share of challenges.

items.title: 'Lightning rod for controversy': History of world's first sex worker statue
items.description: During her short residency in Sydney, the statue of sex worker Joy had many detractors and was even vandalised. Thirty years later, she has returned, with her supporters hoping she will dismantle stereotypes that still plague the industry.

items.title: 'No good reason' for schools to post photos of students on social media: expert
items.description: The independent girls' school in Brisbane is now only sharing what it says are unidentifiable shots of students' faces from the side or behind, due to concerns about image manipulation.

items.title: How a park on the Murray carries our bonds with the Western Front
items.description: A local Australian artist is exploring the bonds between a regional park and its namesake in France as part of an Anzac Day exhibit.

items.title: Cowboy chases dream to make his board game an Aussie classic
items.description: Steve Hawe says he never set out to make a board game — but when inspiration struck, he couldn't ignore it.

items.title: Six dead after gunman opens fire and barricades supermarket in Kyiv
items.description: At least six people have been killed and 14 are injured after a gunman opened fire in the streets of Kyiv.
